configuration.evidence: The independent ROM contains arithmetic and address tables. Test previous ALU-Y as a retained address for ALU-D reads, rather than a constant external byte.
limitations: Every instruction updates the candidate address; real latch qualification is unknown.
The high ROM address bit is fixed per profile, not decoded from the board.

Branch/call indices remain scenario-driven to isolate datapath feedback. Their reconstructed address lookups and these ALU input reads are separate model inputs, not a coherent physical shared-bus model.
Only Am2901 source codes 5,6,7 select D as an operand. The result may still be insensitive to that operand; sampled-but-unselected values are counted separately.
External RAM, DAC strobes, timing and controller links remain unmodeled.

interpretation: Actual ROM bytes supplied to ALU D under assumed address feedback; physical bus and timing not recovered.
